origin: Own exact stochastic single-gene transcription model. The anonymous RNA has no supplied sequence, organism, gene function, experimental construct, intervention recipe or biological engineering target. Stationary means/autocovariances are noiseless constructed oracle moments in one common time unit, not finite-cell measurements or an inference of real biological rate constants. The task concerns identifying a standard promoter-switching model and testing an equilibrium-noise-matched reduction for count-threshold timing.
telegraph_model: A promoter Z(t) in{0,1} switches0->1 at positive k_on and1->0 at positive k_off. Conditional onZ=1, new RNA births occur one molecule at a time at positive r; no births occur forZ=0. Every RNA disappears independently at positive rategamma per molecule. These four rates are time-independent, there is no feedback, division, extrinsic rate mixture, detection loss, maturation lag or other state. Observe the TRUE RNA countN(t), not fluorescence or a thinned sample. All CSV rows belong to this same stationary CTMC. LetC(t)=Cov(N(0),N(t)) including the physical shot-noise contribution atC(0)=Var(N); mean is repeated for source alignment. Regroup rows in increasing lag, retaining all values.
identification: Determine EVERY positive four-rate telegraph parameter solution compatible with the full exact source. A single nonlinear fit is not a global identifiability proof. Derive the stationary first/second and lagged moment equations from the stochastic generator or equivalent exact law. Use the equally spaced lag sequence to construct its complete second-order linear recurrence; audit repeated-pole, zero-amplitude, one-mode and rate-assignment alternatives. Retain actual SolveLinearSystem for recurrence coefficients and for the two-mode amplitudes, and actual PolynomialRoots for every recurrence root. Convert physical roots in(0,1) to continuous-time rates with the correct lag unit, and use the source mean/shot-noise identities to identify which pole is RNA decay. Retain actual MatrixSVD of the3x3 lag HankelH_ij=C((i+j)*0.4),i,j=0,1,2. This Hankel arrangement is not the physical covariance of three sampled times; independently retain actual SymmetricEigenDecomposition of the3x3 Toeplitz covarianceT_ij=C(abs(i-j)*0.4). Explain their different positivity requirements. Report amplitudes paired with ascending continuous decay rates. Explain the remaining positive parameter continuum if only stationary mean/variance were retained; do not use one arbitrary rate solution as a uniqueness claim.
moment_matched_reduction: Build a distinct instantaneous geometric-burst immigration/death model. Independent burst events occur as a Poisson process atlambda; event sizeB is NONNEGATIVE integer geometric with P(B=k)=(1/(1+b))*(b/(1+b))^k,k>=0,meanb. Zero-size events are allowed and cause no count transition; do not count them as an escape from a state. Each RNA still disappears independently at the SAME inferredgamma. Choose positive lambda,b to match the telegraph stationary mean AND variance exactly. Compare both third FACTORIAL moments E[N(N-1)(N-2)] and the full observed autocovariance. This reduction is a mathematical competitor, not assumed to be the fast-switching limit of the fitted finite-rate promoter.
first_passage: For both models, let tau=inf{t>=0:N(t)>=12}, with initial RNA countN(0)=0. For the telegraph model compare three distinct initial promoter laws: (i) stationary promoter MARGINAL P(Z=1)=k_on/(k_on+k_off), chosen independently of the prepared zero RNA count; (ii) the ACTUAL stationary joint process conditioned on observingN=0, P(Z=1|N=0); and(iii) known inactiveZ=0. Case(i) is not automatically case(ii). Infer case(ii) from the same telegraph stationary law. At ordered times[0.5,2,5] return P(tau<=t) for each telegraph initial law and the matched burst model. Also return all four corresponding mean first-passage times. Threshold crossing includes overshoot by any burst size>=12-n; do not discard the infinite burst tail or reflect it at a cutoff.
exact_stopped_process: Construct exact stopped finite CTMCs retaining all states withn=0..11 and one absorbing HIT state. Telegraph state order is(0,OFF),(0,ON),(1,OFF),(1,ON),...,(11,OFF),(11,ON),HIT, dimension25. Burst state order0,1,...,11,HIT, dimension13. Use row generators Q_ij=rate fromi toj, row sums0, exp(tQ)_ij=transition probability. No promoter transitions leave the aggregated HIT state. Retain actual MatrixExponential for EACH complete stopped generator atEACH requested time, and actual MatrixInverse of minus EACH transient24x24or12x12 subgenerator to compute mean first-passage times. Propagate actual returned matrices into the requested initial mixtures and check generator signs, every row sum, probability nonnegativity/normalization, absorption flux and the backward mean-time residual. Explain why these stopped generators are exact for tau despite an unbounded underlying RNA process; a mesh/truncation convergence assertion is insufficient.
stationary_law_and_long_time: Derive or verify the full stationary telegraph RNA count law and the stationary burst law needed to computeP(N>=12), including all counts below12, normalization and a controlled positive-series/quadrature or exact special-function evaluation. State any integral support and parameter conventions. Independent exact moment identities should check the third factorial moment. You may use the standard beta-Poisson representation for the telegraph marginal once its parameters are derived, but promoter stateZ is NOT independently Bernoulli given an observed RNA count. Recover P(Z=1|N=0) from the stationary master equation/joint law rather than substituting its marginal. Distinguish stationary one-time tail probability from eventual first-passage probability. Prove the eventual hit probability and finite mean in both exact stopped models with positive inferred rates. Keep all scientific conclusions within the stated anonymous stochastic model.
required_evidence: Full source acquisition; actual recurrence/amplitude linear systems, complete recurrence roots, Hankel SVD and physical Toeplitz spectrum; complete derived telegraph/burst generators; six actual full-matrix exponentials and two actual transient inverses; full stationary-law and posterior-initialization audit; all source/factorial-moment, probability, backward-equation and global-identification checks belong in the trajectory. The generator entries must come from inferred source rates and the declared geometric tail, not an arbitrary matrix printed with an answer. A method matching only stationary moments is not evidence that threshold dynamics match.

interpretation_proposals.A: Stationary RNA mean and variance can leave a continuum of positive promoter/rate models, while time-resolved covariance can add identifiable rate information.
interpretation_proposals.B: A lag Hankel arrangement of covariance values must be positive semidefinite just like a physical Toeplitz covariance matrix.
interpretation_proposals.C: A reduction matching equilibrium mean and variance need not preserve higher factorial moments or first-passage times.
interpretation_proposals.D: A stationary promoter marginal remains the correct promoter distribution after conditioning on zero RNA.
interpretation_proposals.E: Aggregating all first-hit/overshoot outcomes into an absorbing state can give an exact finite first-passage generator.
interpretation_proposals.F: Geometric bursts larger than the count cutoff can be discarded because the transient generator is finite.
interpretation_proposals.G: Eventual threshold hitting and a stationary one-time count exceedance are distinct probabilities.
interpretation_proposals.H: Model identifiability from constructed noiseless moments establishes rate precision for an unobserved real gene or experimental assay.

reporting: Use the supplied JSON answer schema. Rates per common source time unit; covariance in count-squared, factorial moments in count-cubed, times in source units. All inferred positive solutions must be counted; all probability/time arrays ordered as specified. Absolute tolerance1e-7 for rates, amplitudes, moments and probabilities,1e-6 for mean times. Integer counts/ranks and boolean/ID claims exact. Probability bounds[0,1] and nonnegative times are physical conditions, not relaxed by numeric tolerance. Do not add unrelated nested explanation fields; full derivations and actual receipts remain in the trajectory.

primary_context.title: Markovian Modeling of Gene-Product Synthesis
primary_context.role: Primary source for promoter-state Markov birth/death modeling and stationary/transient gene-product statistics. This task uses own anonymous parameters, exact covariance oracle, competing reduction and threshold queries; no article figures or empirical measurements are copied.
